# Independent audit: homothetic support minorants and common-vertex domination

Audited **candidate 24467ade6f021ae8**, all Sections 1--5. Result: **PASS**. No correction is required.

1. **Finite minorant and sign.** Actual containment gives
   \(\min_{K_j}u\le\sum_p\lambda_p\min_{K_p}u\), so the sampled scalar values
   \(\ell_p=u\cdot c_p-a r_p\) satisfy the convex, rather than concave, anchored inequality. The displayed Farkas certificate has precisely the correct sign for an affine minorant. Normalizing its nonzero nonnegative multipliers gives the stated contradiction. Boundary bases and deficient affine rank need no extra regularity.

2. **One normal, one adjusted tilt.** Rearranging the minorant gives
   \(u\cdot(c_p-c_j)\ge a(r_p-r_j)+b\cdot(p-j)\).
   Since \(u\cdot v=-a\), the comparison translation \((r_j-r_p)v\) has projection \(a(r_p-r_j)\). Thus the margin of the actual affine comparison cap agrees exactly with the pointwise lower margin of the original cap under their common \(K\)-parameter. Both source parameterizations have Jacobian \(r_p^d\). This proves fiberwise, and hence total, cap-mass domination without averaging different tilts.

3. **Compatibility of the comparison.** The original inclusion and ordinary Brunn--Minkowski give \(r_k\ge\sum_p\lambda_pr_p\) at every compatibility target \(k\). With the proof's chosen anchor \(j\) held fixed, the translation \(r_jv\) is constant across the comparison family. Because \(0\in K-v\), radius nesting gives the required inclusion at \(k\). The distinction between these two indices is retained. The exact-hull claim for lattice-convex \(P\) follows by applying that inclusion to every section representation; no full ambient dimension is asserted when the base span is deficient.

4. **A fixed target family despite varying original normals.** For a simplex, a minimizing support point may be chosen as a vertex. The affine vertex permutation taking \(v_0\) to \(v\) fixes the centroid zero, so it is linear, maps \(K\) onto itself, and has determinant of absolute value one. The map
   \(x\mapsto A^{-1}(x-r_jv)\) sends every comparison fiber to the same fixed family \(r_p(K-v_0)\), and sends the comparison point zero to the correct target centroid \(-r_jv_0\). It preserves base coordinates and every closed halfspace. Dependence of this proof map on the original normal and anchor does not affect the conclusion: every original cap is bounded below by the depth at one prescribed point of the same target family.

5. **Boundary and scope.** Pure base-normal caps have identical whole-fiber masses and require no minorant. Parallel translation reduces a containing cap to a through-point cap. Positive-dimensional cut boundaries have zero source volume, while whole boundary fibers in a base-normal cap remain included. The comparison is for the corresponding own-fiber centroids, not for the unrestricted maxima over continuous candidates. Its vertex-transitive-polytope extension uses exactly the same volume-preserving automorphism argument. No OC estimate or positive-normal equal-coefficient reduction is assumed.

The proof is algebraic and applies to all finite supports satisfying the displayed compatibility. No numerical verifier or unproved compactness claim is needed for this audit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
